spans.s:
Śikṣā
(‘instruction [in phonetics]’)
------------------------------------------
An understanding of the वेदस् is quite a tough job, primarily due to two factors: the archaic language and its phonetic system. That is why a study of the six Vedāṅgas—subsidiary sciences that help in understanding the Vedas—is often insisted upon while undertaking a study of the वेदस्.
The very first of the six वेदाङ्गस् is शिक्षा. Its main purpose is to teach the correct pronunciation and intonation of the Vedic mantras of the Saṁhitās. One peculiar feature of the Vedic mantras is that they are divided in several ways leading to what are known as पदपाठ, क्रमपाठ, जटापाठ and घनपाठ (See GHANAPĀṬHA for details.).
The breaking of a compound word (with intonation marks) into the constituents of a पदपाठ depends entirely on the chanting marks like उदात्त, अनुदात्त and स्वरित (See ANUDĀTTA for details.). Different notes on the same compound word can lead to different ways of breaking it and hence different meanings! An oft-quoted example in this regard is the wrong intonation of the word indraśatruḥ by त्वष्टा (the ड़थेर् of वृत्रासुर). As a result, the word used in the oblation of offerings into the consecrated fire meant ‘one to whom इन्द्र is an enemy,’ instead of the one intended, viz., ‘one who is an enemy of इन्द्र’.
This Vedāṅga is very ancient. Its subject matter is found in some of the ब्राह्मणस् and the उपनिषद्स् also.
In the Taittirīya Upaniṣad (1.2) it has been referred to briefly. This science of शिक्षा has six parts: वर्ण (letter of the alphabet); स्वर (pitch or intonation); mātrā (syllabic instant or measure of time); बल (stress or emphasis); sāma (medium mode of pronunciation); and, santāna (juxtaposition or combination).
The varṇas or letters of the Sanskrit alphabet are 63 or 64 according to the शिक्षा, taking the three svaras (udātta etc.) into consideration.
Mātrā refers to the three kinds of time duration: hrasva (one syllabic instant); dīrgha (two syllabic instants); and pluta (three syllabic instants).
Bala (stress applies to the place of production of the sound of the alphabet by the flow of air and the effort needed, both external and internal. There are further subdivisions in these.
Sāma (medium mode of pronunciation) should produce faultless and sweet pronunciation.
Santāna is the same as uniting two words as per the rules of सन्धि, described in the works on grammar.
The extant शिक्षा works are:
Pāṇinīya Śikṣā on the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda;
Vyāsa Śikṣā for the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda;
Yājñnavalkya Śikṣā for the Śukla Yajurveda;
Nāradīya Śikṣā for the Sāmaveda;
Māṇḍūkīya Śikṣā for the Atharvaveda.
Recently 32 works on Śikṣa have been procured from various sources and printed.
See also PRĀTIŚAKHYA.
